open_questions: Centroid not conclusively on_target due to no clear difference image at Tmag 13.77 – ground-based time-series centroid or high-resolution photometry can confirm on-target.

Transit depth scatter drives diff_sigma and sector_oe_max_sigma=4.275 with sectors_over_3=2 – all transits should be checked for depth consistency and secondary/odd-even with higher SNR to rule out EB at twice period.
dossier.public_summary: A steady ~1% flat-bottomed dip repeats every 13.4 days on a small M-dwarf and fits the star's size with a 4-Earth-radius planet size. No neighbour close enough to mimic it was found and no secondary or odd-even difference is seen, so a planet on the target is the best explanation, pending confirmation that the centroid is on-target.

reasons.why: Depth is steady between sectors; each with several transits. Despite bright-star noise warning, no sector-to-sector change argues against a blend/variable causing different depths by aperture.

Significantly flat-bottomed signal with duration consistent with the host (TIC 0.3481 Rsun, Gaia FLAME 0.367334246635437 Rsun) for a central/high-impact transit. Flat shape positively favours planet over grazing binary.
